niche_preference_profile: This user most often prefers interfaces with stronger visual hierarchy, clearer emphasis on primary actions, and structured card-based layouts. They frequently like dark navy/high-contrast themes with bright accent colors, but this is not absolute because they also prefer light neutral themes when those layouts are more organized, breathable, and easier to scan. Across examples, they consistently favor polished grouping, rounded components, compact but well-structured information presentation, clearer active states, and reduced decorative clutter. They also prefer integrated, flatter loading states over floating modal-like loading cards.

top_7_criteria.description: Prefers stronger, more intentional color themes with higher contrast—most often dark navy backgrounds with bright blue/teal/purple accents and white cards, though sometimes light neutral palettes win when they improve clarity and balance.
Prefers interfaces where the most important content and actions are clearly emphasized through contrast, prominent headers, stronger primary buttons, and clearer top-level grouping.
Prefers modular, clearly separated card-based sections over flatter lists, oversized hero graphics, or weakly structured layouts.
Prefers efficient information density, but only when content remains organized and scannable; tends to reject both overly sparse layouts and cluttered/busy arrangements.
Prefers polished UI components with rounded corners, subtle borders, contained icons, and refined control styling rather than harsher, flatter, or less finished elements.
Prefers simpler compositions with fewer unnecessary decorative elements, less redundant labeling, and less visual noise, while still keeping useful structure and emphasis.
Prefers controls and status indicators with obvious active/selected states, such as filled chips, badges, progress bars, labeled navigation, and cohesive accent-colored links/buttons.
